chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Yahya al-Khaza'i, from his father Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and informed him that a boy had been born to me. He said: 'Did you not name him Muhammad?' I said: 'I have done so.' He said: 'So do not beat Muhammad, nor insult him. May Allah make him a delight of your eye during your lifetime and a true successor after you.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, in which profession should I place him?' He said: 'If you keep him away from five things, then place him wherever you wish.'

Do not make him a money-changer, for the money-changer is not safe from usury. And do not make him a seller of coffins, for the owner of coffins rejoices in the plague when it occurs. And do not make him a food trader, for he is not safe from hoarding. And do not make him a butcher, for mercy is stripped from the butcher. And do not make him a slave trader, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The worst of people is the one who sells people.'

key_terms.قُرَّةَ عَيْنٍ: Delight of the eye (source of joy)

ai.seo_question: What are the five professions a Muslim should avoid for their children according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines five professions to avoid for his son Muhammad to preserve moral integrity, linking each to a specific spiritual or ethical danger: money-changers risk usury (riba), coffin sellers may rejoice in calamity, food traders risk hoarding (ihtikar), butchers lose mercy (rahma), and slave traders are deemed the worst of people. This guidance reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual impact of one's livelihood, ensuring that daily economic activities do not erode character or disconnect the individual from divine mercy.
